findings.title: #1152's migration lands as a standalone commit with zero test coverage, before the test commit
findings.evidence: git log ffb629d73..HEAD --stat shows commit 6ee02513d ('fix(db): #1152 the accrual register reads a page at a time (0365)') adds 575 lines of production SQL and touches no test file at all; the only test file (packages/db/tests/accrual-register-pagination.test.mjs) is added in the SEPARATE, following commit 05aad4851 ('test(db): #1152 ...'). WORK-ORDER.md rule 4 requires vertical slices — 'one test -> see it red for the right reason -> the minimal code that turns it green' and 'a commit that adds a whole battery of red cells before any implementation is that anti-pattern' — and the reverse (a whole implementation committed with no test in the same commit) is the same horizontal-slicing failure mode in the opposite direction: the commit history alone gives no evidence a red test preceded this 575-line body.
findings.mitigating_context: The ticket's own report ('A NULL-propagation bug my own tests caught') and the migration's redo evidence (CLARA_MIGRATION_REDO=0365_accrual_register_pagination, documented in packages/db/README.md's ## 0365 section) show the migration WAS in fact exercised against real tests and fixed before the final commit was made -- the local dev loop was red/green even though the two commits were not interleaved. This exact split (migration-only commit, then a separate test-only commit) is also the established pattern for the immediately preceding ticket in the same family: #1075/0334 (commit 705520ed9 'fix(db): #1075 ...', followed by c6355d4ef 'test(db): #1075 ...'), so this is a repo-wide db-ticket convention this worker followed rather than a defect unique to this lane. The migration file's own §0/§T are themselves executable structural assertions (prestate pins, tail census) that run and fail at every apply -- the 'structural cell overrides /tdd' carve-out WORK-ORDER rule 4 grants may reasonably cover the migration file itself, leaving the .test.mjs file as the vertical-slice layer, which IS test-first evidenced by the documented redo.
findings.required_fix: None required for this ticket given precedent; worth a house-law clarification (in WORK-ORDER.md or packages/db/README.md's conventions section) on whether a migration's own structural §0/§T cells satisfy rule 4's red-green loop on their own, so future db tickets and reviewers are not left inferring it from commit messages.
